thread:
incidents-bot: INCIDENT detected: high GPU saturation in tenant pool 'aurora-prod' (single-tenant). 98% GPU utilization, queue depth spike, increased tail-latency. Link: https://console.redwood/incident/3955552468 :rotating_light:

incidents-bot: Severity: SEV2 — customer-facing outage risk. Pager routed to oncall-sre and infra.

devon (oncall-sre): ack — I'm on it. pulling logs + querying autoscaler. @raj @maria @sophie please standby, customer paging us.

devon (oncall-sre): current snapshot:
```
pool: aurora-prod
queued_requests: 820
gpu_util_pct: [95, 97, 98, 99]
avg_latency_ms: 1420
errors_5xx/min: 32
failed_allocs: 14
```

maria (prod-eng): thanks. autoscaler shows no new nodes launched — pool is configured with burst=false (contracted dedicated capacity). Burst buffer = 0.00. No autoscaling headroom.

raj (infra): confirm — this tenant has reserved nodes only. policy: reserved=16 gpus, max_burst=0. If we enable cross-tenant bursting we'll pull from shared-spot which may violate customer isolation unless aurora opts in. Options: emergency-burst-override, temp-provision extra dedicated nodes (cloud request ~20-30m + billing approval), model swap to smaller quantized variant, or soft rate-limit non-critical workloads from aurora.

sophie (support): Aurora Systems on-call just DM'd support — they're seeing timeouts on their /v1/generate endpoints and some 503s. CTO is on the call. They asked for ETA and whether we can restore servicing for critical flows. They also asked whether this is a platform-wide problem (it's not).

devon (oncall-sre): ok immediate plan:
1) propose emergency cross-tenant burst to shared-spot for next 45m to drain queue (requires aurora consent).
2) while burst active, pin aurora's heavy models to q4_small to reduce per-token GPU memory (non-breaking change).
3) throttle low-priority inference (batch jobs, evals) for that tenant.
I'll drive the burst toggle if we get authorization.

elaine (sales): looping in legal/comms? Aurora legal will want written confirmation. I can get verbal okay while we follow up in writing. They want minimal risk of co-tenancy but prefer restored service asap.

raj (infra): running pre-check for burst override: verifying capacity in shared-spot pool...
```
> curl -s https://infra-api/spot/pools/available?region=us-west-2
{"available_gpus": 48, "pending_preemptible": 2}
```
Looks like we have spare spot GPUs. Risk: preemption noise, slightly higher variance.

devon (oncall-sre): pinging aurora on the support ticket: "we can enable temporary cross-tenant burst into a shared pool for 45 minutes while we reduce model footprint — please confirm OK for temporary co-location (we'll provide mitigation and an audit trail)."

sophie (support): aurora response: "Verbal OK from CTO for temporary measure. They want status updates and that we do not route unrelated customers to host their traffic."

raj (infra): executing burst override with safeties (rate limit non-aurora customers out of shared pool). Command:
```
# enable-burst --tenant aurora-prod --pool shared-spot --max-gpus 20 --duration 45m --restrict-to-tenant true
POST /ops/burst  { tenant: "aurora-prod", pool: "shared-spot", gpus: 20, dry_run: false }
```
Response: 202 Accepted.

ops-bot: action: burst override initiated by raj. Token: brst_yyy. Audit link: https://console.redwood/ops/requests/brst_yyy

devon (oncall-sre): enabling throttles for background jobs on aurora to preserve the burst budget.

maria (prod-eng): initiating model-pinning to quantized variant. curl snippet:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood/models/pin \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
 -d '{"tenant":"aurora-prod","model":"aurora-core","target_variant":"aurora-core-q4_small"}'
```
Response: 200 OK — pin applied. Estimated mem drop per replica ~30%.

devon (oncall-sre): queue is draining — now queued: 210. avg_latency_ms: 540. errors_5xx/min: 5.

sophie (support): relaying to aurora: "We enabled temporary shared capacity and reduced model footprint. We're seeing latency improvement. We'll keep you posted every 10m."

elaine (sales): customer says thanks, but asks for confirmation that we will not do this automatically in future without explicit consent. I'll note in the account.

raj (infra): note: billing/finance will need to approve emergency add-on for the extra gpus used during the override. I'll create the billing ticket.

devon (oncall-sre): partial mitigation in place. next steps: keep burst active until queue <= 50 and tail latency < 500ms for 3 consecutive minutes; if spike recurs, consider provisioning dedicated nodes (longer timeline). schedule postmortem with product+infra+sales+support.

incidents-bot: escalation: infra-oncall paged.

ops-bot: telemetry: new nodes allocated from shared-spot: 12 gpus attached to aurora-prod. CPU/GPU metrics in dashboards.

maria (prod-eng): double-checking that no other tenants are using the shared nodes. We set tenant isolation flag true during attach.

devon (oncall-sre): 25m after override — queue: 34, avg_latency_ms: 210, errors_5xx/min: 0. Good. We'll start ramping down the burst at +40m.

sophie (support): aurora happy with current perf and asked for a written incident summary and next steps. They also requested whether we can add a soft autoscaling contract for future surges.

elaine (sales): I'll start a commercial conversation for a burst add-on and discuss soft autoscaling in contract amendment.

raj (infra): initiating controlled drain of shared gpus back to pool in 10m. Command:
```
# disable-burst --request brst_yyy --grace 600
```
Response: scheduled.

devon (oncall-sre): handing off monitoring to raj for the next hour. I'm going to sleep-handoff to follow ops rotation. devon -> raj :point_right: :wave:

raj (infra): ack — taking post-handoff watch. I'll watch errors and queue. If we see >10% CPU/GPU again we'll reopen.

ops-bot: burst brst_yyy ended at +44m. final stats: consumed 9 gpus average across window, peak 15. Queue peak 820 -> reduced to 0 by end.

maria (prod-eng): reverting pin when stable? recommend keep pinned for 6 hours to avoid thrash. will coordinate with aurora.

sophie (support): final update to aurora: "Service restored. We used temporary shared capacity with your approval and decreased the model footprint; no user data left the tenant. We are scheduling a post-incident review and will propose contract-level options to avoid recurrence."

devon (oncall-sre): incident status: mitigated — customer traffic within SLA tolerance but on degraded throughput profile. severity downgraded to SEV3. Postmortem owners: devon (SRE), raj (infra), maria (prod-eng), elaine (commercial). ETA for postmortem: tomorrow 1400 UTC.

devon (oncall-sre): closing thread — if anyone sees any regressions ping me directly. :thumbsup:
